articles.title: ConComp: Constraining and compensating latent representations for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
articles.abstract: Semi-supervised learning has significantly advanced medical image segmentation under limited annotation scenarios. However, existing semi-supervised medical image segmentation (SSMIS) methods based on consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling may be affected by internal covariate shift (ICS), which may disturb feature stability and reduce pseudo-label reliability during training. In this work, we investigate how ICS affects feature stability and pseudo-label reliability in SSMIS. Based on this analysis, we propose ConComp, a unified framework that mitigates ICS from a statistical perspective by introducing distribution-aware latent constraints and compensating for latent distribution discrepancies. Specifically, we introduce a Distribution-Aware Feature Constraint (DAFC) mechanism that derives distribution-aware latent constraints from unlabeled feature statistics and residually integrates them into labeled features, thereby reducing changes in their distributions during training. In addition, we propose a Latent Distribution Discrepancy Compensation (L2DC) mechanism that treats the discrepancy between labeled and unlabeled representations as an informative signal to guide feature fusion, thereby compensating for missing structural cues and improving generalization. Extensive experiments on three challenging SSMIS benchmarks, including BraTS2019, LiTS2017, and Pancreas-NIH, demonstrate that ConComp consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/1jayyang/ConComp.

articles.title: Unsupervised monocular endoscopic depth estimation and overestimation.
articles.abstract: This work finds a new phenomenon of depth overestimationd→∞ in unsupervised monocular endoscopic depth prediction. We theoretically analyze the impact of a photometric consistency constraint loss widely used to measure the photometric inconsistency between two continuous endoscopic video frames during training. To resolve this overestimation problem, we propose a new deep unsupervised learning architecture of structure-valid mask transformer with a new unsupervised training strategy to simultaneously predict monocular depth and pose, without annotating any clinical endoscopic data. Specifically, this architecture employs dense convolution and hierarchical transformer to encode multiscale local and global features, and uses residual attention to effectively fuse or decode these features. More interestingly, structure-valid masks are generated by effective motion-driven photo-difference to establish a new hybrid loss function with photometric structure-aware consistency and 3D geometric consistency for unsupervised training of our proposed model. Consequently, our methods can also deal with weak textures (structures) and illumination variations in monocular endoscopic video images. We evaluated our methods on both public synthetic-labeled and in-house clinical endoscopic video images, with the comprehensive experimental results showing that our unsupervised learning methods can attain critically higher depth accuracy than state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models, as well as more reasonable depth distributions and texture details in predicted depth maps. Our source code has been publicly released on https://github.com/WKFan2026/SVMT.

articles.title: Distribution matching based personalized federated learning for multi-center, cross-modal liver image registration.
articles.abstract: In clinical liver MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging are commonly used and complementary sequences, particularly for liver tumor diagnosis and assessment. Accurate registration between the two modalities facilitates subsequent quantitative analysis and multi-modal image-based evaluation. Although deep learning has achieved remarkable progress in image registration, considerable challenges remain in multi-parametric liver imaging, mainly due to substantial contrast differences, pronounced respiratory motion, limited single-center training data, and inter-center heterogeneity. This study proposes a cross-modal registration framework for liver DWI and DCE across multi-center datasets. First, a multi-task synthesis-registration network (SynReg) is introduced, which integrates image synthesis and registration within a unified architecture to reduce cross-modal appearance discrepancy and facilitate deformable registration. To further improve personalized learning under cross-center heterogeneity, we propose a personalized decentralized distribution matching (PDDM) framework with SynReg as the backbone. PDDM performs compatibility-aware selective collaboration by identifying compatible external training cases and constructing client-specific collaboration relationships. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions are used as a lightweight compatibility descriptor, while the synthesis components remain local and the registration network is selectively aggregated among compatible clients. The framework was evaluated on six datasets collected from five medical centers and acquired on MRI systems from three vendors under both low- and high-b-value settings. PDDM consistently achieved more favorable registration performance than single-center training and representative personalized federated learning methods, while remaining closely competitive with centralized pooled-data training. In comparisons with alternative matching strategies, PDDM showed the most consistently favorable overall performance across centers, b-value settings, and registration metrics. These findings support compatibility-aware selective collaboration as an effective strategy for personalized multi-center liver image registration. Code will be available at https://github.com/ZIC-skyzrc/PDDM-SynReg.

articles.title: The rules of actionable reporting.
articles.abstract: Actionable reporting in radiology is a concept that has gained traction since its inception in 2014. The notion is simple: radiology reports should easily translate into clinical action, particularly when the study is abnormal. This is not so simple. But the process of producing an actionable report is as crucial as the report itself. The process should result in a radiology report that consistently results in information being provided to the referrer that results in improved patient care. This review article presents an evidence-based critique of the concept, demonstrates the numerous pitfalls, illustrates points of gold-standard practice (illustrated as 'Rules') and presents a coherent model of the overall process of actionable reporting, which flanks the crucial central element of an actionable report. KEY POINTS: Question The actionable reporting process is highly dependent on cooperation and coordination of many healthcare staff, IT systems, and different departments, with the radiologist at the heart of it; it should be seen as a multistep process where each step is crucial and interdependent with the overall goal of better patient outcomes via better systems of work. Findings The skilful production of an actionable report is central to this process and remains the responsibility of the individual radiologist. Critical relevance statement Fundamentally, actionable reporting represents the current best practice in radiology reporting. It should be the goal of every radiologist to ensure their reports are actionable and their reporting workflow matches that of actionable reporting.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Bridging Intravenous Thrombolysis in the "Drip-and-Ship" Model for Anterior and Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The drip-and-ship paradigm extends access to endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) from primary stroke centers (PSC), particularly where comprehensive stroke centers (CSC) are limited, but transfer may delay reperfusion. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) before transfer for EVT in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026 for studies comparing IVT versus no IVT in patients transferred from PSC to CSC for EVT consideration. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Heterogeneity was quantified by I2 and prediction intervals (PI). RESULTS: Sixteen observational studies involving 5,488 patients were included. In anterior circulation stroke, IVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (mRS 0-2; aOR 1.76; P=0.02; 95% PI 0.67-4.63, including the null) and lower 90-day mortality (aOR 0.52; P<0.0001). In posterior circulation stroke, IVT was associated with lower mortality (RR 0.74; P=0.04), but not improved functional outcomes. IVT was associated with higher early recanalization during transfer in anterior (RR 5.24; P<0.0001) and posterior circulation (RR 17.46; P<0.0001), without significant differences in post-EVT revascularization or intracranial hemorrhage. All included studies were observational, and certainty of GRADE evidence was very low. CONCLUSION: IVT before transfer was associated with higher early recanalization and favorable clinical outcomes, particularly in anterior circulation stroke, without a detected increase in intracranial hemorrhage. Given the very-low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Identified methodological limitations also informed considerations for future research.

articles.title: Clinical utility of temporal subtraction imaging in head CT: a pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Temporal subtraction (TS) imaging highlights interval changes by computing a voxel-wise difference between spatially registered serial CT examinations, converting side-by-side comparison into a single map of change. Although TS head CT has been validated for acute cerebral infarction detection, its application across the broader spectrum of intracranial pathologies has not been systematically described.We present a pictorial review of twelve clinical cases covering hemorrhagic, ischemic, vascular, neoplastic, and degenerative pathologies. TS imaging was particularly effective for lesions near the visual detection threshold, multi-focal interval findings, and bilateral symmetric changes. It also supported exclusion of new lesions in structurally complex backgrounds. Characteristic artifacts from source-image degradation, scanner protocol differences, and retained contrast are also illustrated.TS head CT is a broadly applicable reading aid with potential to improve diagnostic conspicuity across a wide range of intracranial pathologies. Awareness of characteristic artifacts is essential for accurate interpretation.

articles.title: Robots for CT-guided needle insertion: clinical implementation and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

articles.title: Neuroinflammatory and demyelinating disorders in children: demystifying and updating with a focus on myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease.
articles.abstract: Pediatric neuroinflammatory disorders are a heterogeneous group of autoimmune conditions that have evolved rapidly over the past decade and are encountered in both community and specialized pediatric practice. This group can share overlapping features and includes pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS), acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), formally defined by international consensus in 2023 [32]. Advances in imaging techniques, international consensus statements, and improved detection of central nervous system (CNS)-specific autoantibodies have enabled prompt, precise diagnosis of these disorders [2]. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential tool for early identification, differentiation, and diagnosis, enabling early intervention and focused treatment. This review provides an up-to-date clinico-radiological summary of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), emphasizing MRI protocols and advanced sequences for lesion detection and phenotypic differentiation.

articles.title: Automated Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow Quantification in Hydrocephalus Using Phase-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract: Quantitative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis with phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging depends on segmentation and is affected by operator variability. This cohort method-comparison study evaluated whether a flow-aware deep learning (DL) model provides reproducible C2-C3 CSF segmentation and flow quantification compared with repeated manual segmentation. Ten hydrocephalus patients underwent 3-T phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging at C2-C3, with 32 magnitude and phase frames across the cardiac cycle. Three experts and one novice segmented each case twice using semi-automatic software, generating 80 manual annotations. A pretrained flow-aware 2D-UNet generated one fixed automatic segmentation per case. The inference pipeline was deterministic, meaning that repeated processing of the same input with fixed model weights and settings produced identical masks. A multi-expert reference was defined as the arithmetic mean of the expert measurements. Region of interest (ROI) surface area, peak flow amplitude, and stroke volume were compared using mean difference, Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Expert ICC(1,1) was 0.88-0.97 for surface area, 0.97-1.00 for peak flow amplitude, and 0.97-0.99 for stroke volume; novice values were 0.63, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively. Compared with the multi-expert reference, model mean differences were -0.42 mm2 for surface area, -0.00 mL/s for peak flow amplitude, and -0.01 mL for stroke volume, with CCC values of 0.50, 0.87, and 0.86. Bland-Altman limits of agreement were -69.12 to 68.27 mm2, -1.47 to 1.46 mL/s, and -0.34 to 0.31 mL. The model provided rapid, deterministic CSF segmentation with small cohort-level mean differences in peak flow amplitude and stroke volume; however, individual-level agreement with the flow-derived multi-expert reference was lower than for expert and novice segmentations obtained using the semi-automatic workflow.

articles.title: Influence of forehead gap size on eye protection provided by lead eyewear worn over prescription glasses: A Monte Carlo study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to exposure to high levels of scattered ionizing radiation, interventional radiology (IR) physicians have an elevated risk of radiation-induced eye injuries and cataracts. Previous studies have evaluated the protective effects of regular lead glasses and recommended measures to improve radiation protection for the eyes. However, the protective effects of fit-over eyewear-lead eyewear worn over prescription glasses-have not been thoroughly examined. Importantly, a previous study noted that the space required to accommodate prescription glasses may reduce eye protection. PURPOSE: Monte Carlo (MC) simulations were performed to quantify the protective effects of fit-over eyewear and assess the relative effectiveness of adding bottom shields to conventional lead eyewear to improve eye protection. METHODS: Conventional lead glasses comprising front and side lenses and prescription glasses with plastic lenses and titanium frames were modeled. Lead glasses with bottom shields were created by bending the lower edges of the front lenses of conventional eyewear without increasing the total lens area. Three lead lens thickness values were tested: 0.07, 0.5, and 0.75 mm. Using a mesh-type reference computational phantom representing an adult male to simulate an IR physician, MC simulations were performed with a transcatheter arterial chemoembolization setup. The Particle and Heavy Ion Transport code system was used to calculate the radiation dose deposited in each eye-sensitive volume. The distance (d) between the forehead and front lead lens varied systematically. Protective effects were evaluated using the shielding rate (%) calculated as: (1-Dpr/D0) × 100, where D0 is the radiation dose without protection and Dpr is the dose with eye protection. RESULTS: For the eye near the X-ray source (left eye), the conventional models showed shielding rates >50% when the lead thickness was 0.5 or 0.75 mm and d was ≤0.5 cm. The conventional 0.07-mm lead eyewear exhibited shielding rates <50% when d was 0.5 cm, and <26% when d was ≥0.8 cm. However, 0.07-mm lead eyewear with bottom shields maintained approximately 50% shielding when d increased to 1.0 cm. The models using 0.5- or 0.75-mm lead lenses with bottom shields exhibited shielding rates >76% at d = 1.0 cm. Notably, the shielding rates for the right eye were <12% regardless of introducing bottom shields. The right eye doses were 45-48% of the left eye lens dose without protection. CONCLUSION: By quantifying the relationship between the size of the lens gap and shielding rates, this study estimates the protective effects of fit-over eyewear and can help IR physicians select suitable eyewear. Our findings show that fit-over eyewear with bottom shields effectively protects the left eye during posterior-anterior projection. Although introducing bottom shields can improve conventional side-shield models in terms of increased shielding rate for the left eye, the shielding rates for the right eye remained low because of the gap around the nose. Further study of new designs with a shielded covering over the nose may be warranted.

articles.title: Low-dose CT denoising using a diffusion prior via score distillation sampling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but amplifies noise, which can degrade diagnostic reliability. Recent studies have applied diffusion-based models to LDCT denoising and shown promising performance. However, many of these approaches require paired LDCT and normal-dose CT (NDCT) data or dose-specific retraining, and their reconstruction procedures are often strictly coupled to a predefined diffusion trajectory. PURPOSE: This study proposes an optimization-based LDCT denoising framework that uses a pre-trained NDCT diffusion model as an image prior and can be applied across various dose levels without dose-specific retraining. METHODS: We formulate LDCT denoising as an optimization problem guided by a pre-trained score-based generative model (SGM) trained only on NDCT images. The Poisson data fidelity term enforces consistency with the measured projection data, whereas the score distillation sampling (SDS) term acts as a regularizer that guides the reconstruction toward the NDCT distribution learned by the pre-trained SGM. The denoised image is obtained by iteratively optimizing a projection-domain residual variable using the combined Poisson data fidelity gradient and SDS-based regularization gradient. RESULTS: The proposed method effectively suppressed noise while preserving fine anatomical structures across multiple dose levels using a single pre-trained diffusion model. Quantitative evaluations with respect to full-dose reference images and visual comparisons demonstrated competitive performance compared with supervised and self-supervised LDCT denoising baselines. CONCLUSIONS: The results show that diffusion-based image priors can be leveraged across various low-dose levels within the proposed optimization-based denoising framework. Our work suggests that SDS-guided diffusion priors are a promising direction for LDCT denoising in data-limited settings.

articles.title: Model-based image restoration targeting higher-dose digital mammography: Impact on radiologists' detection of clustered microcalcifications.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Image noise in digital mammography (DM) can obscure image details and reduce the detectability of clinically relevant findings such as microcalcifications. PURPOSE: To present and evaluate an extended model-based (MB) image restoration pipeline for DM that incorporates quantum, electronic, and structural noise components, as well as spatial noise correlation, and to assess its effect on breast radiologists' detection of simulated microcalcification clusters in clinical mammograms. METHODS: A total of 120 clinical DM images acquired using a GE Senographe Pristina system were used. Simulated microcalcification clusters were inserted into locally dense fibroglandular regions at controlled contrast levels. The restoration pipeline was configured to target the signal and noise characteristics predicted by the model for an acquisition at approximately twice the original radiation dose. Six breast radiologists with different levels of experience, classified as Junior or Senior, participated in two human observer experiments: (i) a pilot study using original clinical images with simulated clusters and a four-alternative forced-choice (4AFC) protocol combined with a three-down-one-up (3D1U) staircase to estimate reader-specific contrast detection thresholds and achieve comparable baseline task difficulty across readers; and (ii) a main 4AFC observer study using individualized datasets generated according to each reader's estimated contrast threshold, in which microcalcification detection performance was compared between the original and restored image conditions based on the percentage of correct responses (PC). Two generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) were used: the first evaluated the effect of image condition as a fixed effect, with reader and case as crossed random intercepts, and the second evaluated the effect of reader experience on detection performance in the original image condition. RESULTS: At the reader-specific contrast thresholds estimated in the pilot study, the mean PC for the original images was 78.3%, within the prespecified target performance range. Mean PC increased to 84.3% for the restored images, corresponding to an absolute improvement of 6.0 percentage points. The primary GLMM indicated a significant restoration effect on detection performance (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.15-2.14, p = 0.005  ). Baseline mean PC was 78.7% for Junior readers and 78.0% for Senior readers, and the separate GLMM found no evidence of an experience-group effect under the original image condition ( p = 0.858  ). CONCLUSIONS: The proposed extended MB restoration pipeline improved the detectability of simulated microcalcification clusters by breast radiologists under the controlled 4AFC conditions investigated. By targeting the signal and noise characteristics predicted by the model for an acquisition at approximately twice the original radiation dose without requiring additional radiation exposure, the method represents a promising approach for improving microcalcification detectability in DM.

articles.title: DoseRAD2026: A benchmark dataset for AI-accelerated photon and proton dose calculation in radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate dose calculation is a fundamental component of modern radiotherapy, enabling precise tumor irradiation while sparing surrounding healthy tissue. With the increasing adoption of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided radiotherapy and growing interest in real-time adaptive radiotherapy, there is a demand for fast and accurate dose calculation techniques on both computed tomography (CT) and MRI. To facilitate research in this area, the DoseRAD2026 dataset and accompanying challenge introduce a publicly available benchmark dataset comprising paired CT and MRI data with corresponding beam-level photon and proton Monte Carlo (MC) dose distributions, enabling the development and systematic evaluation of advanced dose calculation and prediction methods. ACQUISITION AND VALIDATION METHODS: The DoseRAD2026 dataset comprises paired CT and MRI data from 115 patients (75 training, 40 testing) treated on a hybrid MRI-linear accelerator (MRI-linac) for thoracic or abdominal lesions and is derived from the SynthRAD2025 dataset. Image pre-processing included deformable image registration, air-cavity correction and resampling. Ground-truth photon (6 MV) and proton dose distributions were generated using open-source MC dose calculation algorithms and resulted in a training dataset of 40,500 photon beams and 81,000 proton beamlets. DATA FORMAT AND USAGE NOTES: The dataset is organized into photon and proton subsets, each comprising paired CT-MRI images, beam-level dose distributions, and JSON files specifying patient-specific beam configurations. Data are provided in compressed MetaImage (.mha) format with standardized naming linking dose files to beam parameters in the JSON files. The dataset is released under a CC BY-NC 4.0 license, with the training set available from April 2026 and the test set withheld until March 2030. POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS: The DoseRAD2026 dataset enables benchmarking and development of fast dose calculation methods for radiotherapy applications. Potential use cases include rapid beam-level dose estimation for photon and proton therapy, MRI-based dose calculation in MRI-only and MRI-guided radiotherapy workflows, and support for real-time adaptive radiotherapy strategies.

articles.title: Uncertainty-aware hybrid model for reliable navigation guidance in prostate biopsy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate biopsy - performed under ultrasound (US) guidance - is the only confirmatory procedure for diagnosing prostate cancer. If several systems aiming at improving the accuracy of tissue sampling for histopathological analysis exist, they often fail to adequately account for patient / tissue motion and deformation during the procedure or are not suitable for real-time guidance towards a pre-defined target. PURPOSE: This work proposes a real-time assistance method to help urologists navigate between biopsy sites leveraging both 2D US and 3D US information. METHODS: The proposed hybrid framework combines three ResNet-18-based sub-networks with a Kalman filter to track the pose of the current 2D US frame within a reference 3D US volume acquired during the intervention. Two of the networks predict relative rigid transformations from pairs of US frames or frame/slice combinations extracted from the 3D volume. A third network predicts the registration error from a frame/slice pair and acts as a large-error detector. This error prediction module is integrated directly into the iterative registration process, to ensure robust tracking in the presence of tissue deformation or image artifacts, while also providing an uncertainty estimate of registration quality at each time step. The proposed framework was trained and evaluated on complex biopsy trajectories generated from a dataset of 847 3D US volumes acquired during real transrectal prostate biopsy procedures from 97 patients. The dataset was divided into training (78 patients, 669 volumes), validation (10 patients, 115 volumes), and test (9 patients, 63 volumes) sets. Performance was compared with an image-correlation-based baseline method using clinically relevant evaluation metrics, including the mean surface registration error (mean SRE) over 25-s trajectories, as well as the percentage of registered frames with an SRE below 2.5 mm and 5 mm. Statistical significance was assessed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (adjusted with Holm-Bonferroni correction) and 95% confidence bootstrap intervals (CI 95%) across the test cohort. Effect sizes were quantified with rank-biserial correlation (RBC). RESULTS: Compared with the baseline method, the proposed approach achieved a significant reduction in the mean SRE over 25-s trajectories, decreasing from 3.1  [ 2.2 , 4.9 ]  to 2.2  [ 1.8 , 2.5 ]   mm (median [CI 95%], p = 0.016, RBC = 0.96). In addition, the proposed large-error detector - used for uncertainty estimation - achieved a balanced accuracy score of 0.81 for classifying registration errors above or below a given threshold of 5 mm. CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to improve the accuracy and robustness of real-time prostate biopsy navigation guidance.

articles.title: Intravenous oxycodone versus morphine patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) after uterine artery embolisation: A propensity matched case-control study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The use of intravenous oxycodone is still limited in the Interventional Radiology setting. This study aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of intravenous oxycodone used in patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) after uterine fibroid embolisation (UFE), compared to morphine. METHODS: Retrospective case-control study. The study group consisted of patients treated with UFE between March and December 2024, using an oxycodone protocol. The control group consisted of a previously published dataset using morphine protocol. Primary outcomes were safety and the incidence of severe nausea. RESULTS: There were 57 patients in the oxycodone group compared to 69 in the morphine group. After propensity score matching, this left 43 in the oxycodone group and 60 in the morphine group. Groups were similar in terms of background demographics, however the use of smaller 355-500 micrometre polyvinyl alcohol particles were higher in the oxycodone group (100% vs 18%, p < 0.001).No analgesic-related adverse events were observed in either group. The incidence of severe nausea was lower in the oxycodone group (43.3% vs 37.2%, p = 0.533) despite a higher rate of post-embolisation syndrome (65.1% vs 48.3%, p = 0.091). After multiparametric logistic regression, oxycodone was associated with a 64% reduced odds of severe nausea (OR 0.36, p = 0.217). CONCLUSIONS: Intravenous oxycodone PCA is safe and showed a trend towards a lower incidence of severe nausea compared with morphine PCA. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: There is limited evidence of the use of oxycodone PCA to treat post-embolisation syndrome. This study showed it was safe and resulted in reduced nausea compared to morphine.

articles.title: From Isolated Intelligence to Interpretive Infrastructure in Radiology AI.
articles.abstract: Radiology has more regulatory-cleared artificial intelligence tools than any other medical specialty, yet they have delivered less consistent clinical impact than their benchmark performance suggested. We argue that the dominant response, scaling perceptual models and extending them toward autonomous agency, mistakes the nature of the problem. The limitation is architectural, not algorithmic: current systems perform isolated perception while remaining disconnected from the temporal, contextual, and experiential integration that interpretation requires. We trace this to a fundamental simulation gap, the absence of the counterfactual signal that lets AI reach superhuman performance in other domains, and argue that scaling alone cannot close it. In response, we outline a hybrid orchestration layer, grounded in established clinical frameworks, that assembles a comprehensive evidence base for the radiologist while keeping generative components constrained and interpretive judgment human. The shift is one of design paradigm: from isolated tools deployed alongside the radiologist to interpretive infrastructure that composes validated outputs into coherent evidence without anchoring the reader's own assessment.

articles.title: The b-Value Dependence for Higher-Degree Spherical Harmonic Powers of the Diffusion MRI Signal Follows Stick Model Predictions in White Matter.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the dependence on b-value of the spherical harmonic powers for the diffusion MRI signal in white matter to theoretical predictions from the stick model of water diffusion within axons. METHODS: Diffusion MRI data were acquired at 3 T in three healthy adults with 10 b-value shells (b = 1000-10 000 s/mm2) and 64 directions per shell. For every b-value, the signal was expanded in spherical harmonics for all even degrees l up to l = 6, and the harmonic power for each degree was calculated. These were compared in selected white matter regions of interest to the theoretical predictions of the stick model, which depend on just two adjustable parameters: the intra-axonal diffusivity and an amplitude factor for each degree. The intra-axonal diffusivity was estimated independently using triple diffusion encoding MRI, leaving the amplitude factor as the sole fitting parameter. RESULTS: Close agreement between experiment and theory was found for b  ≳   4000 s/mm2, the threshold where extra-axonal water signal is expected to be strongly suppressed, for total cerebral white matter as well as separately within the genu, body, and splenium of the corpus callosum. These findings extend prior studies that either considered only the l = 0 harmonic power or treated the intra-axonal diffusivity as a fitting parameter. CONCLUSION: In white matter, the b-value dependence of the diffusion MRI signal's even degree spherical harmonic powers up to l = 6 are relatively well-described by the stick model of axons for b  ≳   4000 s/mm2.

articles.title: Camera calibration and tracking for augmented reality during robotic surgery.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Robot-assisted surgery (RAS) offers clinical advantages but remains limited by reduced visualization and lack of tactile feedback. Augmented reality (AR), achieved by overlaying preoperative imaging onto laparoscopic video, may mitigate these challenges. This study evaluates the accuracy and clinical feasibility of an AR system that uses electromagnetic (EM) tracking to determine the position of the robotic endoscope and enable real-time image overlay during surgery. METHODS: For calibration, an EM sensor was rigidly attached to the robotic endoscope and a second sensor to a calibration checkerboard. 35 calibration images were acquired. To determine the required number of calibration images, 2600 random subsets containing 5-30 images were calibrated using RANSAC-based robust estimation and evaluated on 16 separately recorded checkerboard frames using three-dimensional (3D) Euclidean error. Subsequently, a clinically suitable adapter carrying the EM tracker was rigidly mounted on the robotic endoscope and evaluated during 16 robot-assisted pelvic lymph node dissection (RPLND) procedures. RESULTS: Calibration accuracy and robustness improved with increasing dataset size. A dataset of 19 images was the smallest dataset size with a median 3D error within 5% of the best observed performance, with a mean 3D Euclidean error of 0.541 ± 0.060 mm. Using the same protocol, the clinical adapter achieved 0.784 ± 0.075 mm. System evaluation during 16 RPLND provided stable, real-time tracking and AR visualization. CONCLUSION: The proposed calibration and tracking approach enables sub-millimeter AR overlay accuracy while allowing continuous tracking of the robotic endoscope through an externally mounted EM tracker. Its successful use during 16 RPLND procedures demonstrates that the method can be integrated into a clinical robotic workflow and supports real-time visualization without substantial procedural modification. These findings provide a technical foundation for further development and validation of image-guided AR applications in robotic-assisted surgery.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses. RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Myocardial infarction detection framework using cardiac motion estimation with deformable registration field.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Among them, myocardial infarction (MI), which is characterized by abnormal myocardial motion, remains a critically important condition to detect. Accurate diagnosis of MI requires detailed motion analysis; however, motion-based assessment is time-consuming and imposes a considerable burden on physicians. Moreover, most previous studies have relied on local motion descriptors or limited shape features, resulting in suboptimal detection performance. METHODS: To address these limitations, we propose a deep learning framework, termed MambaMorph-Motion Infarction Detector (MMMID), for myocardial infarction detection from cardiac CT images. The proposed pipeline integrates semantic segmentation, sequential deformable registration using MambaMorph, and a DenseNet-based classification module to effectively leverage rich spatiotemporal myocardial motion information across the cardiac cycle. RESULTS: The proposed method enables accurate tracking of myocardial motion aligned with anatomical structures by associating time-resolved motion fields with corresponding CT volumes. MMMID achieved an accuracy of 91.92% and an AUC of 0.9335 on an in-house cardiac CT dataset. Compared with the CT-only configuration, the integration of sequential motion fields improved recall, suggesting that motion information provides complementary diagnostic cues for myocardial infarction detection rather than replacing anatomical CT information. CONCLUSION: The proposed framework enables myocardial infarction detection by jointly leveraging cardiac anatomy and estimated myocardial motion. Although CT appearance remained a strong source of discriminative information, sequential motion fields contributed complementary functional information, particularly for improving sensitivity to infarction cases. MMMID may serve as a supportive tool for automated cardiac CT analysis and could help reduce the burden of motion-based assessment in clinical workflows.

articles.title: Explainable WinDWS-SwinNet: Optimizing Ultrasound Deep Radiomics for Multipathology Breast Lesion Classification.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Timely and accurate characterization of breast lesions into different pathological classes through noninvasive imaging techniques is crucial for early cancer diagnosis and effective patient management. This study aims to develop a novel, explainable attention-based deep network to analyze radiomic patterns for predicting heterogeneous breast cancer types using ultrasound imaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicentric retrospective dataset comprises brightness-mode ultrasound images of breast tissue collected across five different centers/databases. A total of 3256 images, having biopsy-proven 2068 benign and 1188 malignant lesions, were analyzed. A lightweight and computationally scalable network, WinDWS-SwinNet, is developed for binary and multipathology breast cancer classification. An optimized image preprocessing algorithm is proposed to enhance ultrasound radiomic features, thereby improving data generalizability and diagnostic accuracy. RESULTS: The WinDWS-SwinNet architecture demonstrated superior performance in breast cancer classification, achieving an area under the curve of 0.96, an overall test accuracy of 95.79%, and robust class-wise results with 95.11% precision and 98.51% sensitivity for benign tumors and 97.13% precision and 90.86% sensitivity for malignant tumors. For multipathology classification, the model achieved a test accuracy of 93%, with class-wise accuracies ranging from 94% to 99.5%. External validation on the independent unseen dataset resulted in an accuracy of 95.36%, highlighting the robustness and generalizability of the proposed model beyond the training data. CONCLUSION: The developed methodology shows promising results in characterizing breast lesions into pathological subtypes noninvasively, effectively mimicking real-world diagnostic workflows, thereby supporting radiologists in reducing diagnostic uncertainty and enhancing confidence in clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Inferior Vena Cava Filters in Adolescents with Thromboembolic Disease: Technical Outcomes, Retrieval, and the Role of Skeletal Maturity.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage. Retrieval was attempted once the initial indication had resolved and anticoagulation was feasible. RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in every case; mean caval diameter was 17.9 ± 3.0 mm. Retrieval was attempted in 22 of 26 filters and succeeded in 19 (86% of attempts, 79% by intent to retrieve, 73% overall). One successful retrieval required a second attempt with an adjunctive loop-snare maneuver. Median indwelling time was 89 days (range 1-489). All three unsuccessful retrievals occurred at Risser stage 3 or below (3 of 7 versus 0 of 15 attempted; P = .02), not explained by caval diameter (P = .33). Seven filters (27%) remained in situ. No periprocedural adverse events occurred. Both retained filters assessed by CT showed caval wall penetration, one with strut fracture and asymptomatic migration at 16 years; chronic caval occlusion developed in one patient. CONCLUSION: Off-label IVCF placement in adolescents achieved high technical and retrieval success. Retrieval failure was confined to skeletally immature patients and was not explained by caval diameter. Strut fracture with migration at long-term imaging reinforces the need for timely retrieval.

articles.title: From Cell to Circuit: Altered Functional Network Topology in iPSC-derived Neuronal Circuits in Major Depressive Disorder.
articles.abstract: The functional organization of brain networks relies on a delicate balance between segregation and integration, which supports both localized neural processing and global information exchange. While numerous whole-brain imaging studies have linked disruptions in this balanced topology to Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), it remains unclear whether such macroscale alterations are reflected in neuronal circuit dynamics at the cellular level. In this study, we investigated whether neuronal networks derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) of nine MDD patients display a distinct functional topology compared to nine matched controls. We obtained skin biopsies from all participants, cultivated fibroblasts, and reprogrammed these into hiPSCs. We then differentiated hiPSCs into neural progenitor cells (NPCs), which we later developed into neurons. We recorded spontaneous activity in the derived neuronal networks using calcium imaging, and applied graph theory analysis to quantify differences in functional topology between groups. We observed a significant decrease in the clustering coefficient and average node degree in MDD-derived neural networks. Furthermore, global efficiency showed a downward trend across varying thresholds and network sizes in patient-derived lines. Together, these findings demonstrate diminished segregation and reduced overall nodal connectivity in MDD-derived neural networks. This suggests that a predisposition for less efficient functional topology exists in depression at the microscale, highlighting the utility of hiPSC technology in modeling cellular disease mechanisms and exploring potential cellular correlates of network-level phenomena reported in depression.

articles.title: Common Phenomenal and Neural Substrate Geometry in Visual Motion Perception.
articles.abstract: What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive. To overcome the challenge of expressing subjective experience, recent structural and relational approaches have been proposed from mathematics. Yet, as far as we know, no attempts have been made to evaluate the relationship between a certain structure of qualia and the structure of a candidate underlying physical substrate. Towards this ambitious goal of linking the structures of qualia and physical, we set out to make an empirical first step by focusing on experienced dissimilarity of visual motion in human participants and stimulus-evoked neural population response geometry recorded from mouse primary visual cortex. From human participants (N=171), we obtained dissimilarity ratings of visual motion experiences induced by 48 stimuli, spanning across 8 directions and 6 spatial frequencies. Analysis revealed a human dissimilarity structure that was not well captured by a simple monotonic function of physical motion-direction difference alone nor by a pure orientation-symmetry account. From nine individual mice, we recorded single-neuron activity (n=751) with optical imaging in both awake and lightly anaesthetised conditions (isoflurane 0.6-0.8%). From neuron population responses to a similar set of motion stimuli, we computed a distance matrix that is comparable to our human dissimilarity matrix. Quantitative analyses show structural commonalities between a human dissimilarity structure and mouse neural structure, where a categorical organisation of stimulus direction best explained both. These commonalities were similar in awake and anaesthetised recordings, suggesting that this coarse V1 geometry is relatively insensitive to this type of anaesthesia; future work combining behaviour with causal intervention is required to relate such neural structures to conscious experience. Finally, we list several empirical factors that can be improved to promote our qualia structure approach in the future.

articles.title: Photon FLASH spares radiation-induced lung injury and pulmonary hypertension in a preclinical model.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) radiotherapy has shown significant promise in reducing normal tissue toxicities with equivalent tumour control compared to conventional (CONV) dose rates termed the FLASH effect. In this study, we compared radiation-induced lung injury and changes in the pulmonary circulation following localised right lung irradiation at UHDR and CONV exposures using photons. METHODS: Acute and late pulmonary radiation responses were assessed in pneumonitis (C3H/NeJ) and fibrosis prone (C57BL/6) mice. 18 Gy was delivered to the right lung at CONV (0.05 Gy/s), FLASH (76.2 Gy/s) and FLASH split dose (FSD, average 2.6 Gy/s) exposures. Early responses (72 h and 4 weeks after irradiation) were investigated by immunohistochemistry (Ly6G, F4/80), fluorescence staining (EdU) and serum profiling (cytokines and lipid peroxidation assays). Fibrosis was assessed at 30 weeks after irradiation by cone-beam CT (CBCT) analysis and quantification of collagen, senescence (p21) and TGF-β levels. Changes in pulmonary vasculature and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was assessed in C57BL/6 mice at 30 weeks to characterise changes in pulmonary circulation associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH). RESULTS: At early timepoints, UHDR exposures led to reduced immune cell infiltration (neutrophils and macrophages) and tissue damage in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. Serum analysis supported FLASH sparing with decreased levels of markers associated with chronic inflammation and increased markers of tissue repair in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. At 30 weeks after irradiation at a UHDR, the lung parenchyma was structurally similar to controls (p = 0.33) with minimal collagen deposition supported by CBCT tissue density analysis. In contrast, CONV and FSD animals showed significant collagen deposition (p < 0.01) with thickened alveolar septa and reduced alveolar air spaces. UHDR exposures significantly reduced functional and histological metrics of PH (p < 0.05) compared to CONV. CONCLUSIONS: UHDR photons significantly reduce radiation-induced pneumonitis and fibrosis with secondary effects on the pulmonary circulation sparing PH.

articles.title: IAP inhibition enhances response to radiotherapy and chemotherapy in preclinical models of rectal cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The modern management of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) involves sequential radiotherapy and chemotherapy, termed Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT). Although TNT significantly improves tumour regression and achieves complete response rates of approximately 30 %, treatment efficacy remains limited in part by tumour-intrinsic resistance to apoptosis. We therefore sought to investigate the effects of radiotherapy on TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling in rectal cancer and evaluate whether inhibition of Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins (IAPs) could enhance treatment response. METHODS: Transcriptomic profiling was performed on rectal tumour biopsies obtained before and after two weeks of neoadjuvant radiotherapy (n = 42). Gene Set Enrichment Analysis was used to identify pathways altered following radiotherapy. The clinically relevant IAP antagonist, tolinapant, was evaluated in rectal cancer models to assess effects on cIAP1/2 degradation, radiation- and chemotherapy-induced apoptosis, and formation of 5-fluorouracil (5FU)-induced drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells. Mechanistic studies were performed in the presence of TNFα, and in vivo efficacy was assessed in SW837 xenograft models. RESULTS: Radiotherapy induced robust upregulation of TNFα/TNFR1 signalling and apoptosis-associated gene sets. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis confirmed enrichment of both "TNFα signalling via NFκB" and "Apoptosis" pathways. Upregulation of TNF, TNFRSF1A, RIPK1, TRADD, and CFLAR (FLIP) was observed alongside downregulation of DIABLO, suggesting that radiotherapy primes tumours for TNFα-mediated apoptosis but that elevated antiapoptotic signalling may suppress this response. Tolinapant degraded cIAP1/2 and significantly enhanced radiation-induced apoptosis in rectal cancer models. Co-treatment with TNFα further amplified apoptosis through a caspase-8-dependent mechanism. The combination of tolinapant and radiation was well-tolerated in vivo and reduced SW837 xenograft tumour volume compared to radiation alone; however, this difference did not meet statistical significance. Tolinapant also potentiated chemotherapy-induced apoptosis and prevented the emergence of 5FU-induced DTP rectal cancer cells. CONCLUSION: These findings identify TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling as a potential radiation-induced vulnerability in rectal cancer and provide a mechanistic rationale for combining radiotherapy with IAP antagonists. Tolinapant also enhanced apoptosis induced by chemotherapy whilst suppressing drug-tolerant persisters, supporting further investigation of IAP antagonism as a strategy to improve TNT efficacy in the neoadjuvant management of rectal cancer.

articles.title: Preoperative MRI-based clinicoradiological scoring system for perineural invasion prediction and risk stratification in intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A multicenter study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a strong predictor of early recurrence and poor survival in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC). However, PNI can only be confirmed by postoperative histopathology, and preoperative risk stratification tools remain lacking. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 190 intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma patients from three centers were retrospectively allocated into training, internal, and external validation cohorts. Continuous variables were dichotomized via the Youden index. Independent predictors from multivariate logistic regression were assigned integer scores, calculated by dividing each β coefficient by the minimum β, to construct a simplified scoring system. Performance was validated using AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Using the optimal Youden cutoff , patients were risk-stratified to evaluate recurrence-free survival via Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses. RESULTS: Elevated platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (>144.43), perihilar location, and disrupted arterial enhanced edge integrity were identified as independent PNI predictors. Each was assigned 1 point to construct a 3-point scoring system. The system demonstrated favorable discrimination with AUCs of 0.870, 0.859, and 0.807 in the training, internal, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration and DCA confirmed excellent agreement and clinical utility. High-risk patients (score ≥ 2) exhibited significantly shorter RFS across the training (hazard ratio [HR] = 4.150, 95 % CI: 2.343-7.350; P < 0.001), internal validation (HR = 3.801, 95 % CI: 1.589-9.093; P = 0.001), and external validation (HR = 3.311, 95 % CI: 1.397-7.848; P = 0.004) cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: This MRI-based scoring system offers a noninvasive tool to preoperatively identify high-risk PNI patients, potentially guiding extended resection, neoadjuvant therapy, and intensified surveillance.

articles.title: Deep learning classification of benign and malignant adnexal lesions on pelvic MRI.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Despite the recent introduction of O-RADS MRI to standardize MRI assessment of adnexal lesions, diagnostic imaging remains challenging. Artificial intelligence might provide help in radiological decision support. Therefore, we trained deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) for detection and classification of benign and malignant adnexal lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two radiologists (R1/R2) retrospectively assigned MR-O-RADS scores on multiparametric MRI performed in 144 patients (median age 50.2 ± 14.3 years) prospectively included between 11/2016-12/2024 after diagnosis of indeterminate adnexal lesions on transvaginal ultrasound. R1 manually three-dimensionally segmented ovaries/adnexal lesions. Histopathology or 2-year-follow-up served as gold standard. Transverse T2WI, T1WI, T1WI fat-saturated, T1WI post-contrast, DWI and ADC maps were used for further analysis. nnU-Net was trained in 5-fold-cross-validation using three designs: D1) T2WI only at full resolution, D2) all 6 sequences at full resolution, D3) T2WI only downsampled by half in-plane. Prediction performance and specificity of malignant vs. benign entities was evaluated using ROC-AUC methods and the McNemar test for clustered data. RESULTS: The dataset included annotations of 237 ovaries (130 benign and 67 malignant histopathologies, 40 lesions with negative 2-year-follow-up). R1/R2/D1/D2/D3 models achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.96/0.96/0.86/0.86/0.84 (95%CI 0.93-1.00/0.93-1.00/0.81-0.92/0.78-0.93/0.77-0.91), respectively. Cluster-adjusted AUC of R1/2 was significantly higher than D1-D3 models (all p < 0.001). Youden index specificity/sensitivity was 0.95/0.91,0.94/0.93,0.88/0.73,0.90/0.76,0.87/0.76, while it was 0.95/0.91,0.48/0.91,0.39/0.91,0.42/0.91 at the closest operating point to sensitivity ≥ 90%, with specificity of R1/2 being significantly higher than D1-3 models (all p < 0.001). Subanalysis in cases with full agreement between all CNN models demonstrated similar relationships. Subset analysis in frequent histopathologies showed AUCs of 1.0/0.99 (95%CI 1.00-1.00/0.98-1.00) for radiologists and 0.98 (95%CI 0.96-1.00) for model D2. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning models achieved overall validation set performance at AUC ≥ 0.84, lower than the radiologists, however in frequent histopathologies D2 achieved AUC = 0.98, not statistically different from R1/2, suggesting that training with more examples especially of infrequent histopathologies may further increase performance.

articles.title: Incorporating visceral adipose tissue into dual-region deep learning radiomics on CT improves preoperative lymph node metastasis prediction in gastric cancer: A multicenter study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is associated with tumor progression in gastric cancer (GC), but its added value for predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM) remains unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to construct a DR-DLR model that incorporates CT-based features from both VAT and tumor, with the goal of predicting LNM in GC patients, while investigating its biological relevance. METHODS: 855 GC patients were retrospectively collected across three clinical centers, divided into a primary cohort, one internal test cohort, and two independent external validation cohorts. An Attention Residual Transformation Network (ARTNet) extracted imaging representations from CT images. Feature representations and clinical variables were integrated using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to build the DR-DLR model. Model performance, generalizability, prognostic value, and biological relevance were evaluated using internal/external testing, radiologist comparison, survival analysis, and radiogenomics analysis. RESULTS: Incorporation of VAT-derived features improved predictive performance compared with tumor-only models. The DR-DLR model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95 % CI: 0.817-0.946), 0.834 (95 % CI: 0.743-0.897), and 0.848 (95 % CI: 0.775-0.901) in the internal and two external test cohorts, respectively. It outperformed junior and senior radiologists in LNM assessment. Overall survival was shorter in high-risk patients than in low-risk. Radiogenomics analysis revealed that the high-risk phenotype was associated with activation of immune-related pathways and increased infiltration of CD4 + T cells, plasma cells, dendritic cells, and mast cells. CONCLUSION: The DR-DLR model improved LNM prediction, with its high-risk phenotype linked to immune-related molecular alterations, supporting its value for preoperative risk stratification.

articles.title: Multiparametric imaging with dynamic 18 F-FDG PET shows increased breast glucose metabolism in patients with breast cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Multiparametric PET separates tracer signal into bound and free fractions via reconstructions that reflect the net trapping rate (Ki) and apparent distribution volume (DV). This study aimed to investigate differences in background parenchymal uptake (BPU) between patients with and without breast cancer using multiparametric PET and to evaluate differences in primary tumor uptake according to hormone receptor status. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included female patients (n = 48) with newly diagnosed breast cancer and 146 patients without breast cancer. Patients with breast cancer under or after treatment and patients with bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Enrolled patients underwent whole-body dynamic PET and three quantitative indices representing BPU (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], Ki and DV) were calculated. The primary tumor uptake was calculated between estrogen- or progesterone-receptor-positive and -negative groups. RESULTS: The mean SUVmax, Ki and DV of breast cancer cases were 1.39 ± 0.352, 4.88 × 10 - 3 ± 1.61 × 10 - 3 and 24.2 ± 15.4 respectively, whereas in control cases, mean SUVmax, Ki and DV were 1.10 ± 0.320, 3.96 × 10 - 3 ± 1.25 × 10 - 3 and 17.1 ± 10.8 respectively (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004). The areas under the curve from the ROC analysis for breast cancer presence were calculated as 0.727, 0.681 and 0.653 respectively. In addition, age-stratified analysis showed that SUVmax and Ki were significantly higher in patients with breast cancer than in patients without breast cancer. Regarding the primary tumor uptake, Ki was significantly higher in the estrogen receptor-positive group. CONCLUSION: Multiparametric PET revealed that pure glucose metabolism is significantly elevated in the background mammary glands of patients with breast cancer, and the Ki in the primary tumor is associated with ER status. Dynamic PET imaging may be a useful imaging biomarker for the development of breast cancer.

articles.title: Prospective evaluation of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation for refractory ventricular tachycardia: initial clinical experience in Japan.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This prospective study evaluated the 1 year safety and efficacy of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) delivered using the CyberKnife system for refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in Japanese patients, in accordance with a prespecified clinical protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three male patients with radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA)-refractory VT and structural heart disease, namely hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), were enrolled. A single fraction of 25 Gy was delivered to the target volume defined by multimodal image fusion. The primary endpoint was the absence of Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events within 12 months. RESULTS: The primary endpoint was achieved, with no acute or subacute Grade ≥ 3 toxicities observed in any patient during the first year. Although all patients experienced a reduction in VT burden, the clinical course differed by etiology. Cases 2 (DCM) and 3 (ICM) showed typical responses, including delayed efficacy and late recurrence requiring repeat RFCA. In contrast, Case 1 (HCM), with a substantially larger target volume (133 mL), showed a rapid response but a progressive decline in left ventricular ejection fraction by myocardial scintigraphy, from 59.7% to 40.0%, during the 24 month extended follow-up. CONCLUSION: STAR demonstrated preliminary feasibility as a noninvasive salvage therapy for refractory VT in this initial Japanese pilot experience. However, the late functional decline observed in Case 1 highlights the need for long-term follow-up and myocardium-sparing techniques for large target volumes. (jRCTs042230030).

articles.title: Beyond Chronologic Age: What Digital Breast Tomosynthesis Performance Tells Us about Screening across the Lifespan.
